newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close at highest since May 1994.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close at highest since May 1994.

text.p: French shares closed at a fresh high on Friday, taking the blue-chip CAC-40 index to its highest close since May 1994, after a series of U.S. data this week, ending with the trade data on Friday, was well received.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 19.90 points or 0.92 percent at 2,185.23 while the CAC-40 October futures contract was up 23 at 2,190.
On May 18, 1994, the CAC-40 closed at 2,183.99 on it has been below that level until today.
* Volume was 5.8 billion francs of which 4.1 billion in blue-chip shares.
* Investors appeared to be reasssured that Thursday's national strike by public sector employees "was no big deal," said a head of equity sales at a French broker.
* Lagardere, closed 0.97 percent higher at 166.20, after having suffered from some profit-taking during the day, building on Thursday's run of more than 20 percent.
Its bid for state-owned Thomson SA gave analysts a peg to consider stock valuations and revived the "value" theme in assessing companies.
* Lagardere's finance committee director Philippe Camus said the company did not plan spinoffs or asset sales, following market talk it could hive off defence from publishing activities.

* Danone falls 1.73 percent to 738 francs on disappointment over nine-month sales. Danone said on Thursday after close its nine-month sales were up two percent on a like-for-like basis. Broker Cheuvreux de Virieu lowered its recommendation on Danone to sell from buy.
* SGS-Thomson gains 3.32 percent on third quarter results. Morgan Stanley upgraded to strong buy from outperform.

* Michelin fell 1.95 percent to 250.90 after the company decided to buy back its convertible bonds at a price below the market price -- causing the conversion of bonds in to shares followed by the sale of shares by bond investors.
* The CAC-40 index also hit an intra-day high for the year at 2,187.07. The index gained 1.7 percent compared to last Friday, with falls on Monday and Wednesday.
* Dealers said they expected profit-taking next week with a support level for the October future contract seen at 2,160.
